decisions.question: How should the coordinator handle long-running tasks that exceed a single Claude session? (Context window ~200k tokens; pipeline runs 30-120 min)

options.label: Checkpoint/resume via orchestrator state (coordinator resumes from pipeline state after crash)
Sliding context window with periodic state snapshots
Fixed-duration sessions with automatic handoff
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: Should coordinator-driven pipelines operate within the existing phase system (REFINE/PLAN/IMPLEMENT/PR with dynamic selection), outside it (freeform execution with a new permission model), or in a hybrid mode (phases are advisory)?

options.label: Within existing phases (coordinator selects/skips phases but gateway enforces phase permissions)
Outside phases (new freeform execution model with coordinator-specific permissions)
Hybrid (phases advisory; coordinator can skip/reorder; gateway uses coordinator-scoped permission set)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: What should the coordinator be able to do without human approval?

options.label: Spawn agents and manage workflow only (all PRs and external actions need approval)
Spawn agents + create PRs without approval (only merges need human)
Full autonomy within guardrails (spawn, PR, comment — only merge blocked)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How much of the coordinator system should be built in the first iteration?

options.label: Coordinator agent + orchestrator API extensions only (no MCP, CLI-triggered)
Coordinator + MCP server (interactive mode via Claude Code)
Coordinator + MCP + async triggers (Slack/webhook/GitHub events)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.question: How should users interact with the coordinator?

options.label: Slack commands (post task in channel, receive updates)
Claude Code session with MCP tools (conversational, interactive)
Dedicated egg CLI command (e.g. egg-coord submit)
GitHub issue labels/events (label triggers coordinator)
Other (explain in reply)

questions.question: What cost limits or guardrails should be applied to coordinator sessions? (e.g., max agents per task, max total token budget, max wall-clock time)
What should happen when the coordinator session crashes mid-task with running agents? (e.g., agents continue/pause/escalate)
